title: AGGREGATE: a total that says what to ignore

docs.syntax: =AGGREGATE(function-number, options, range) with 9 for SUM, 1 for AVERAGE and 6 to skip error values
docs.explain:
AGGREGATE takes three arguments: a function number, an options number, then the range. The function number works as it does in SUBTOTAL, so 9 adds and 1 averages. The formula =AGGREGATE(9,6,B2:B4) adds the three prices to 35.

The options number decides what the calculation walks past. Six ignores error values, and seven ignores hidden rows as well. A plain SUM answers a broken reference with that same error across the whole column, while AGGREGATE keeps adding the cells that still hold numbers.

The cost of option six is that a failed row disappears from the total. Here B2:B4 is intact, so 35 is the plain sum as well. The second screen changes only the function number, to 1, and rounds 35 over 3 to 11.7.

errors.text: The options number is not one AGGREGATE recognises, so it cannot decide what to skip.
The function number is outside the range AGGREGATE supports.
Option six has left a failed row out of the total, so the sum is one row short.

docs.atWork: A total that keeps working when one row of the source data has broken.
docs.outcome: Write a three-argument aggregate and know which cells the options number leaves out.
docs.teaches: AGGREGATE's function number, options number and range, in that order
docs.dataset: Stock list where the total has to survive a broken row

screens.prompt: In D5, add the prices up so that a broken cell in the range would not stop the total.

hints.syntax: =AGGREGATE(9,6,B2:B4): function number, options number, range, in that order.
hints.func-aggregate: Three arguments, and only AGGREGATE carries the options number that skips a broken cell.
hints.require-ref: The range is the price column of the table.
hints.value: Ten plus five plus twenty is 35.
hints.error: The total is divided by zero after the aggregate runs, so #DIV/0! is what shows.

reject.why: a plain SUM gives up on the whole range when one cell breaks
the last price is left out of the range
function number one averages the prices instead of adding them
the range starts one row late
the total is divided by zero
the range sits outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In D5, average the prices with AGGREGATE and round the answer to one decimal place.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(AGGREGATE(1,6,B2:B4),1): the aggregate sits inside the ROUND.
hints.func-aggregate: An average over a range that may hold a broken cell needs AGGREGATE, with 1 as its function number.
hints.value: 35 divided by 3 is 11.666..., which rounds to 11.7.
hints.error: With the divisor at zero the cell returns #DIV/0!, and the rounding never happens.

reject.why: one broken cell would make AVERAGE return an error instead of a number
the average is left unrounded at eleven and two thirds
function number nine adds the prices instead of averaging them
the first price is missing from the average
the average is then divided by zero
the aggregate falls outside the parentheses ROUND needs

seo.title: AGGREGATE in Excel: skip errors in a total
seo.description: AGGREGATE takes a function number, an options number, then the range. Option 6 ignores error values, so one broken cell no longer kills the whole total.
